verdict.headline: Qatar keeps talking to Iran as Washington readies Gulf allies for a possible strike after the vote
verdict.label: Saturday: S&P 500 closed Fri at 7,579.97 (-1.82%), Nasdaq 25,437.00 (-2.86%); VIX 19.42; 10Y ~4.91%; DXY 101.92; Brent (Dec) $117.64; BTC ~$77,517 Sat (+0.9% in 24h).
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: no stock, bond or oil market has traded since Friday. Qatari mediators held more than 12 hours of talks in Tehran on Friday and planned to continue in Doha on Saturday, while Iran's foreign minister said there are no plans to meet US officials. The Wall Street Journal reported that Washington told Gulf allies to prepare for a short, intense campaign after Tuesday's midterms. The tanker mine claims that circulated Saturday date to Thursday and were already in Friday's prices. Binance said it has covered up to 90% of the $6.3 billion stolen and plans to resume withdrawals Sunday.

What it means: Brent's expiring contract settled at $117.64, 71 cents under its $118.35 wartime high, with Hormuz flows already more than 40% below the prewar level, so oil enters the week priced for risk rather than relief. A 5.51% I bond rate and 3.7% September CPI explain why December hike odds held at 72.7% through Friday's bond rally.

What would change the picture: a confirmed date for US-Iran talks would remove some of oil's premium, and a strike announcement after the vote would test $118.35. A 10-year back above 5.11% before Friday's jobs report would mean oil's inflation risk had overtaken the demand for safety; AMD's Tuesday results test whether Intel's miss spreads to the chip sector.
verdict.lede_short: Nothing but crypto has traded since Friday, and the weekend's question is whether the US strikes Iran again after Tuesday's vote: Qatar is still mediating, while Washington has told Gulf allies to prepare for a short campaign. Brent ended Friday 71 cents under its wartime high, so oil starts the week priced for risk. A set date for US-Iran talks would ease that; a 10-year back above 5.11% before Friday's jobs report would mean oil, not the tech selloff, is setting rates.

supporting_data.label: Qatari mediators held more than 12 hours of talks in Tehran on Friday and planned to continue in Doha on Saturday, but Iran's foreign minister said there are no plans to meet US officials — diplomacy is active but has no date that oil can price.

The Wall Street Journal reported that the US told several Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense campaign against Iran after the November 3 midterms — the main risk to oil's Sunday open sits on the other side of Tuesday's vote.

Hormuz crude flows fell to 7.3 million barrels a day in the week to Wednesday, more than 40% below the prewar level, after at least 30 vessels were hit in October — any renewed strike would start from an already reduced supply route.

Treasury set the new I bond rate at 5.51%, with a 1.40% fixed portion that is the highest since 2006, as September CPI ran 3.7% — the inflation backdrop that kept December hike odds at 72.7% even as bonds rallied on Friday.

Binance said it has covered up to 90% of the roughly $6.3 billion stolen and plans to resume withdrawals Sunday — bitcoin near $77,517 has held above Friday's $76,176 low, and Sunday's outflows are the next test.

Intel drew downgrades to neutral from Bank of America, Roth and Seaport after its 29% fall, though its data center and AI revenue rose nearly 80% to $7.3 billion — the miss came from PCs and production limits, not AI demand.
